answers.responseText: No. Multiplying two n-bit streams requires remembering on the order of n bits of partial product, growing without bound as the inputs grow, but an SC has a fixed set of MEM blocks and therefore only finitely many internal states.

I would add unbounded, re-readable memory — an external store the circuit can write, move through, and read back later — instead of a fixed set of MEM blocks. That is exactly the step from an SC to a Turing Machine.

No. Intelligence requires connecting the past to the present — learning, planning, even recognizing that a situation has changed. A being with no memory could only react reflexively to the current stimulus, like a CC turbot that cannot count its own steps.
